name: St. Mary Catholic Church
history: Wilmington's first Catholic church, St. Thomas the Apostle, was built in 1846-47. Rafael Guastavino designed St. Mary's, begun in 1908; he died that February, and his son carried on. The first service was held on 17 December 1911, and Cardinal James Gibbons dedicated it as pro-cathedral on 12 April 1912. It became a diocesan shrine in 2005 and a basilica in 2013.
arch: Spanish Baroque in brick and tile, famous for Guastavino's self-supporting tile vaulting and dome, built, per its National Register nomination, without structural steel, wooden beams or nails.
features: It served as pro-cathedral of North Carolina's Catholic jurisdiction before the Diocese of Raleigh was formed.

look.d: Guastavino's patented thin-tile vaulting holds itself up.
Built after the master's death by his son.

fun: The Guastavino tile system was used in Grand Central Terminal and Ellis Island too.
journal: Father designed, son finished. Tiles stacked into a sky over Wilmington.

quiz.q: Who finished the church after Guastavino's death?
What is its dome made of?
